For all the testimonies of the faith are linked together, and one is rendered more credible by another, nay, is in some manner made clear, and is judged more plain and reasonable. [[1:17|as it is written: The just man liveth by faith|Sicut scriptum est : Justus autem ex fide vivit]]. The Apostle adduces this to prove that the justice of God is revealed in the Gospel, or in the Christian, from faith unto faith.

paras.t: Sed quum fides sit una, juxta illud, Unus Dominus, una fides, unum baptisma : quomodo nunc dicitur, Ex fide in fidem, quasi sint fides diversæ ? Et respondendum, quod fides est una ex parte objecti. Numeratur autem et diversificatur ex parte subjectorum : in eodem tamen fides non est nisi una numero, sicut et caritas. Unde, ut dictum est, per fidem intelligitur actus fidei, qui diversificatur. — Auctoritas vero ab Apostolo introducta, habetur in Habacuc, ubi legitur : Ecce qui incredulus est, non erit recta anima ejus in semetipso ; justus autem in sua fide vivet. Cui concordat illud quoque Isaiæ : Qui incredulus est, infideliter agit. Unde in Ecclesiastico inducitur : Qui timetis Dominum, credite illi, et non evacuabitur merces vestra. Nullus etenim proprie justus est, nisi referat opera sua ad ultimum finem, qui est supernaturalis felicitas. Hunc autem finem non agnoscimus, nisi per fidem, quæ in omni actu meritorio dirigit rationem. Idcirco in fide, tanquam in basi seu fundamento virtutum, vivit justus. Hinc etiam ait Scriptura : Domine, oculi tui respiciunt fidem.
paras.en: But since faith is one, according to that word, [[Eph 4:5|One Lord, one faith, one baptism|Unus Dominus, una fides, unum baptisma]], how is it now said, *from faith unto faith*, as though there were different faiths? The answer is that faith is one on the side of its object; but it is numbered and diversified on the side of its subjects; yet in one and the same person faith is only one in number, as is charity also. Hence, as was said, by *faith* is understood the act of faith, which is diversified. — The authority brought in by the Apostle is found in Habacuc, where we read: [[Hab 2:4|Behold, he that is unbelieving, his soul shall not be right in himself: but the just shall live in his faith|Ecce qui incredulus est, non erit recta anima ejus in semetipso ; justus autem in sua fide vivet]]. With this agrees also that of Isaias: [[Is 21:2|he that is unfaithful dealeth unfaithfully|Qui incredulus est, infideliter agit]] [the printed margin reads Is. xxi, 2]. Hence it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 2:8|Ye that fear the Lord, believe him: and your reward shall not be made void|Qui timetis Dominum, credite illi, et non evacuabitur merces vestra]]. For no one is properly just unless he refers his works to the last end, which is supernatural happiness. But this end we know only by faith, which directs reason in every meritorious act. Therefore the just man lives in faith, as in the base or foundation of the virtues. Hence too the Scripture says: [[Jer 5:3|O Lord, thy eyes are upon truth|Domine, oculi tui respiciunt fidem]] [the Vulgate has *fidem*, faith, which Denis follows; the Douay-Rheims renders it *truth*].

paras.t: Porro, quod ex fide sit salus justitiaque credentium, declarat consequenter Apostolus ex opposito. Revelatur enim ira Dei, id est justa ultio divinæ justitiæ, de cœlo, per revelationes cœlestes ab angelis factas, qui hominibus divinam districtionem ac ultionem, seu pœnas inferni, revelaverunt. Vel, Ira Dei de cœlo, id est Dei cœli, seu Dei cœlestis, de quo canitur, Laudate Dominum de cœlis ; vel, Dei judicis, de cœlo venturi ad judicandum vivos ac mortuos. Vel dicitur ira Dei revelari de cœlo, quia in die novissimo cœli ardentes (secundum Petrum apostolum), et angeli cum Judice venientes, ostendent iram Dei contra iniquos. Itaque revelatur ira, indignatio, detestatio Dei, super omnem impietatem, qua peccatur in Deum, et injustitiam, qua peccatur in proximum, hominum perversorum, eorum videlicet qui veritatem Dei quam agnoscunt, hoc est divinorum notitiam, seu divinam justitiam, quæ frequenter veritas nominatur, in injustitia detinent, id est, injuste vivendo apud se retinent, non procedentes in actum virtutis, sed ipsam veritatem ab operis executione retrahunt atque abscondunt : quibus competit illud, Scienti bonum et non facienti, peccatum est illi ; et illud, Melius erat non cognoscere viam justitiæ, quam post agnitionem retrorsum reverti. Hoc loco incipit loqui Apostolus contra peccata gentilium idololatrarum. De hac revelatione iræ Dei super impietatem et injustitiam hominum, ipse Dominus per Prophetam protestatur : Visitabo super orbis mala, et contra impios iniquitatem ipsorum ; et requiescere faciam superbiam infidelium, et arrogantiam fortium humiliabo.
paras.en: Further, that the salvation and justice of believers is from faith the Apostle next shows from the opposite: [[1:18|For the wrath of God|Revelatur enim ira Dei]] [[1:18|is revealed|Revelatur]], that is, the just vengeance of the divine justice, [[1:18|from heaven|de cælo]], through heavenly revelations made by the angels, who have revealed to men the divine severity and vengeance, or the pains of hell. Or, *the wrath of God from heaven*, that is, of the God of heaven, or the heavenly God, of whom it is sung, [[Ps 148:1|Praise ye the Lord from the heavens|Laudate Dominum de cœlis]]; or, of God the Judge, who will come from heaven to judge the living and the dead. Or the wrath of God is said to be revealed from heaven because on the last day the burning heavens (according to Peter the apostle)[[2 Pet 3:12||]], and the angels coming with the Judge[[Matt 16:27||]], will show forth the wrath of God against the wicked. So the wrath, indignation and abhorrence of God is revealed [[1:18|against all ungodliness|super omnem impietatem]], by which sin is committed against God, [[1:18|and injustice|et injustitiam]], by which sin is committed against one's neighbour, [[1:18|of those men|hominum eorum]], perverse men, namely of those [[1:18|that detain the truth of God|qui veritatem Dei]] which they know, that is, the knowledge of divine things, or the divine justice, which is often called truth, [[1:18|in injustice|in injustitia detinent]], that is, by living unjustly they keep it shut up within themselves, not going forward into the act of virtue, but withdrawing and hiding the truth itself from being carried out in deed. To them applies that word, [[Jas 4:17|who knoweth to do good and doth it not, to him it is sin|Scienti bonum et non facienti, peccatum est illi]]; and that, [[2 Pet 2:21|better for them not to have known the way of justice than, after they have known it, to turn back|Melius erat non cognoscere viam justitiæ, quam post agnitionem retrorsum reverti]]. Here the Apostle begins to speak against the sins of the idolatrous Gentiles. Of this revelation of the wrath of God against the ungodliness and injustice of men the Lord Himself protests by the Prophet: [[Is 13:11|And I will visit the evils of the world, and against the wicked for their iniquity: and I will make the pride of infidels to cease, and will bring down the arrogancy of the mighty.|Et visitabo super orbis mala, et contra impios iniquitatem eorum; et quiescere faciam superbiam infidelium, et arrogantiam fortium humiliabo.]].

paras.t: Insuper causa punitionis istorum subjungitur. Quia quod notum est Dei, hoc est, quod per naturalem rationem de Deo sciri potest, videlicet quod Deus sit justus et sapiens, approbans bona et reprobans mala, et quod ipsi soli sit cultus perfectissimus, utpote honor latriæ, exhibendus, manifestum est in illis, hoc est, gentilibus notum fuit. Deus enim illis revelavit per influentiam luminis naturalis, per quod anima rationalis ex creaturis intelligit Creatorem. De quo lumine scriptum est : Signatum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Domine. Unde Origenes ait : Notum Dei, est hoc quod ex mundi hujus dispositione et naturali ratione assequi possumus ; ignotum vero Dei, est ratio substantiæ ejus, quæ omnem latet creaturam, similiter et mysterium humanæ liberationis. Pluribus autem modis Deus revelavit hominibus veritatem, videlicet per sapientiæ infusionem, per angelicam revelationem, per Sanctorum instructionem, per naturalem rationem. Secundum Damascenum quoque, omnibus naturaliter inserta est cognitio exsistendi Deum. Nunc tamen agit Apostolus de revelatione quæ fit per naturalem rationem, quæ ex creaturis ascendit ad Creatoris notitiam.
paras.en: Moreover the cause of their punishment is added: [[1:19|Because that which is known of God|quia quod notum est Dei]], that is, what can be known of God by natural reason, namely that God is just and wise, approving good and condemning evil, and that to Him alone the most perfect worship, namely the honour of latria [the worship due to God alone], is to be shown, [[1:19|is manifest in them|manifestum est in illis]], that is, was known to the Gentiles. [[1:19|For God hath manifested it unto them|Deus enim illis manifestavit]] [Denis reads *revelavit*, revealed] through the inflowing of natural light, by which the rational soul understands the Creator from creatures. Of which light it is written: [[Ps 4:7|The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us|Signatum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Domine]]. Whence Origen says: What is known of God is that which we can attain from the ordering of this world and by natural reason; but what is unknown of God is the nature of His substance, which is hidden from every creature, and likewise the mystery of man's deliverance. God has revealed the truth to men in several ways: by the infusion of wisdom, by angelic revelation, by the instruction of the Saints, and by natural reason. According to Damascene also, the knowledge that God exists is naturally implanted in all. Here, however, the Apostle treats of the revelation made through natural reason, which rises from creatures to the knowledge of the Creator.

paras.t: Subditur namque : Invisibilia enim ipsius, id est divina natura incorporea, simplex et invisibilis, et perfectiones ejus quæ naturaliter sciri possunt, videlicet justitia, potentia, providentia, etc., quæ dicuntur invisibilia Dei, quoniam licet sint unum in Deo et ipsa divina essentia, tamen secundum rationem distinguuntur, diversimode significantur, et per diversa cognoscuntur. Hæc ergo invisibilia Dei, a creatura mundi, id est ab homine, qui inter creaturas hujus sensibilis mundi primatum sortitur : de quo Dominus dicebat, Prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ, id est omni homini ; per ea quæ facta sunt, id est per res creatas, intellecta, id est intellectualiter contemplata : oportet enim invisibilia Dei intellectuali puroque oculo intueri ; conspiciuntur, id est, agnoscuntur. Vel, Per ea quæ facta sunt intellecta, id est per creata rite considerata. Sempiterna quoque virtus ejus, id est æterna potestas Dei, et divinitas, ab homine conspiciuntur per ea quæ facta sunt, non utique per speciem, vel quid sint, sed quia sunt, et quid non sunt. Quum enim omnis creatura sit quidam radius sui creatoris, et omnis effectus sit quædam participata similitudo suæ causæ, quoniam unumquodque producit sibi simile : hinc certum est quod ex naturis creatis aliquo modo cognoscatur increata natura. Videntes quippe philosophi ordinem esse in rebus, et quod unum procedit, causatur et gubernatur ab alio, pervenerunt ad notitiam unius primi summique entis, quod oportuit esse æternum, perfectum et independens. Et uniformi quoque motu cælestium corporum, et stabili consistentia mundi atque gubernatione inferiorum a superioribus, perpenderunt esse in universo unum quemdam summum provisorem, dominatorem ac principem. Quam multa autem vera, profunda ac mira agnoverint Plato cum suis, et Aristoteles cum Peripateticis, de invisibilibus Dei, de sempiterna virtute ac divinitate ipsius, patet in libris eorum. Sed et Proclus Platonicus in Elementatione sua theologica, de Deo atque divinis subtilissime loquitur, quamvis in multis aberret. Prædictis autem verbis Apostoli consonat illud quoque Sapientis : A magnitudine speciei creaturæ poterit creator horum cognoscibiliter videri. Omnia enim, ut Salomon ait, propter se ipsum operatus est Dominus, scilicet ut in creaturis divina majestas atque perfectio refulgerent, sicque ex consideratione creaturarum incitaretur homo ad contemplationem, amorem, ac reverentiam Creatoris. Hinc scriptum est : Fecit Deus opera sua ut timeatur ; et iterum, Levate in excelsum oculos vestros, et videte quis creavit hæc.
paras.en: For it is added: [[1:20|For the invisible things of him|Invisibilia enim ipsius]], that is, the divine nature, incorporeal, simple and invisible, and His perfections that can be known naturally, namely justice, power, providence, etc., which are called the invisible things of God because, though in God they are one and the divine essence itself, yet they are distinguished in concept, are signified in different ways, and are known through different things. These invisible things of God, then, [[1:20|from the creation of the world|a creatura mundi]], that is, by man, who holds the first place among the creatures of this sensible world, of whom the Lord said, [[Mark 16:15|preach the gospel to every creature|Prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]], that is, to every man [Denis takes *a creatura mundi* as *by the creature of the world*]; [[1:20|by the things that are made|per ea quæ facta sunt]], that is, through created things, [[1:20|being understood|intellecta]], that is, contemplated intellectually, for the invisible things of God must be beheld with the pure eye of the intellect; [[1:20|are clearly seen|conspiciuntur]], that is, are known. Or, *understood by the things that are made*, that is, by created things duly considered. [[1:20|His eternal power also and divinity|sempiterna quoque ejus virtus, et divinitas]], that is, the eternal might of God, are seen by man through the things that are made, not indeed in their proper form, or what they are, but that they are, and what they are not. For since every creature is a kind of ray of its creator, and every effect is a certain participated likeness of its cause, since each thing produces its like, it is certain that from created natures the uncreated nature is in some way known. For the philosophers, seeing that there is order in things, and that one thing proceeds from, is caused and governed by another, came to the knowledge of one first and highest being, which must be eternal, perfect and independent. And from the uniform motion of the heavenly bodies, the stable consistency of the world, and the governance of lower things by higher, they judged that there is in the universe one supreme provider, ruler and prince. How many true, profound and wonderful things Plato with his followers, and Aristotle with the Peripatetics, knew of the invisible things of God, of His eternal power and divinity, is plain in their books. And Proclus the Platonist too, in his Elements of Theology, speaks most subtly of God and divine things, though he errs in many points. With these words of the Apostle agrees also that of the Wise Man: [[Wis 13:5|by the greatness of the beauty, and of the creature, the creator of them may be seen, so as to be known thereby|A magnitudine speciei creaturæ poterit creator horum cognoscibiliter videri]]. For, as Solomon says, [[Prov 16:4|The Lord hath made all things for himself|Omnia enim, ut Salomon ait, propter se ipsum operatus est Dominus]], namely that the divine majesty and perfection might shine forth in creatures, and so man might be stirred by the consideration of creatures to the contemplation, love and reverence of the Creator. Hence it is written: [[Eccles 3:14|God hath made that he may be feared|Fecit Deus opera sua ut timeatur]]; and again, [[Is 40:26|Lift up your eyes on high, and see who hath created these things|Levate in excelsum oculos vestros, et videte quis creavit hæc]].

paras.t: In tantum igitur cognoverunt Deum, ita ut sint inexcusabiles de suis peccatis, præsertim de idololatria. Non enim excusat eos ignorantia. Quia quum cognovissent Deum per naturalem rationem, secundum modum prætactum, non sicut Deum glorificaverunt, serviendo ei cum debita reverentia, aut gratias egerunt Deo pro beneficiis suis ; sed evanuerunt, hoc est, inanes effecti sunt, in cogitationibus suis vanis ac frivolis, glorificantes et magnipendentes se ipsos ; et obscuratum, luce gratiæ privatum, et splendore divinæ sapientiæ destitutum, est insipiens cor eorum, impletumque est caligine vitiorum, propter vanitatem cogitationum suarum. Unde scriptum est : Væ qui cogitatis inutile. Et alibi admonet Dominus : Auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis. Per Salomonem quoque Sapientia Dei, Christus Dominus, contestatur : Ego, inquiens, Sapientia habito in consilio, et eruditis intersum cogitationibus.
paras.en: So far, then, did they know God, [[1:20|so that they are inexcusable|ita ut sint inexcusabiles]] for their sins, especially for idolatry; for ignorance does not excuse them. [[1:21|Because that, when they knew God|Quia cum cognovissent Deum]] by natural reason, in the manner touched on above, [[1:21|they have not glorified him as God|non sicut Deum glorificaverunt]], by serving Him with due reverence, [[1:21|or given thanks|aut gratias egerunt]] to God for His benefits; [[1:21|but became vain|sed evanuerunt]], that is, were made empty, [[1:21|in their thoughts|in cogitationibus suis]], vain and frivolous, glorifying and making much of themselves; [[1:21|was darkened|et obscuratum]], deprived of the light of grace and bereft of the splendour of divine wisdom, [[1:21|And their foolish heart|est insipiens cor eorum]], and was filled with the gloom of vices, because of the vanity of their thoughts. Whence it is written: [[Mich 2:1|Woe to you that devise that which is unprofitable|Væ qui cogitatis inutile]]. And elsewhere the Lord admonishes: [[Is 1:16|take away the evil of your devices from my eyes|Auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis]]. By Solomon also the Wisdom of God, Christ the Lord, bears witness, saying: [[Prov 8:12|I, wisdom, dwell in counsel, and am present in learned thoughts|Ego … Sapientia habito … intersum cogitationibus]].

paras.t: Dicentes enim se esse sapientes, id est, se ipsos de sua sapientia jactantes, atque in se ipsis, non in fonte sapientiæ gloriantes, stulti facti sunt coram Deo seu divino judicio, qui stultam fecit sapientiam hujus mundi. Qui enim scientiam creaturarum et naturalem sapientiam divinorum non ordinat ad salutarem ac supernaturalem sapientiam, et Dei honorem, veraciter stultus est, tanquam contra ordinem rerum faciens, et contra censuram æternæ sapientiæ agens. Propter quod scriptum est : Stultus factus est omnis homo a scientia sua ; et iterum, Sapientia tua et scientia tua decepit te ; et rursus, Væ qui sapientes estis in oculis vestris. — Sed videntur hæc de philosophis verificari non posse. Quum enim quidam interrogasset Pythagoram, an sapiens esset, dixit se sapientem non esse, sed philosophum, id est sapientiæ amatorem. Et ejus exemplo posteri ejus se non vocaverunt sapientes, sed philosophos. Et respondendum, quod licet non dicerent ore, corde tamen dicebant se sapientes, paucissimis forsan exceptis, qui nec idola coluerunt : de quibus modo non agitur.
paras.en: [[1:22|For, professing themselves to be wise|Dicentes enim se esse sapientes]], that is, boasting of their own wisdom and glorying in themselves, not in the fountain of wisdom, [[1:22|they became fools|stulti facti sunt]] before God or in the divine judgement, who has [[1 Cor 1:20|made foolish the wisdom of this world?|stultam fecit sapientiam hujus mundi]]. For he who does not order the knowledge of creatures and the natural wisdom of divine things to saving and supernatural wisdom and to the honour of God is truly a fool, as acting against the order of things and against the verdict of the eternal wisdom. Therefore it is written: [[Jer 51:17|Every man is become foolish by his knowledge|Stultus factus est omnis homo a scientia sua]]; and again, [[Is 47:10|Thy wisdom, and, thy knowledge, this hath deceived thee|Sapientia tua et scientia tua decepit te]]; and once more, [[Is 5:21|Woe to you that are wise in your own eyes|Væ qui sapientes estis in oculis vestris]]. — But it seems this cannot be verified of the philosophers. For when someone asked Pythagoras whether he was wise, he said he was not wise but a philosopher, that is, a lover of wisdom; and following his example his successors called themselves not wise men but philosophers. The answer is that though they did not say it with their mouth, yet in their heart they said they were wise, except perhaps a very few who did not worship idols, of whom there is no question here.

paras.t: Et mutaverunt gloriam incorruptibilis Dei, in similitudinem imaginis corruptibilis hominis, id est, cultum, honorem et gloriam immortali et invariabili Deo impendendam, exhibuerunt imaginibus, statuis seu idolis hominum mortuorum, et volucrum, et quadrupedum, et serpentium. Quam verum sit hoc, in libro Sapientiæ prolixe describitur. Quomodo etiam populus Judæorum tanto errori subjacuit, talpasque ac vespertiliones adoravit, Isaias atque Ezechiel prosequuntur. Quidam autem gentilium ipsas imagines, quidam vero res significatas per imagines coluerunt.
paras.en: [[1:23|And they changed the glory of the incorruptible God into the likeness of the image of a corruptible man|Et mutaverunt gloriam incorruptibilis Dei, in similitudinem imaginis corruptibilis hominis]], that is, the worship, honour and glory to be paid to the immortal and unchangeable God they showed to images, statues or idols of dead men, [[1:23|and of birds, and of fourfooted beasts and of creeping things|et volucrum, et quadrupedum, et serpentium]]. How true this is is described at length in the book of Wisdom[[Wis 13:1||]] [the margin gives Wis. xiii–xv]. How the people of the Jews also fell into so great an error and worshipped moles and bats, Isaias and Ezechiel relate[[Is 2:20||]][[Ezech 8:10||]]. Some of the Gentiles worshipped the images themselves, others the things signified by the images.

paras.t: Propter quod, id est propter idololatriam jam prædictam, quæ omnis peccati origo efficitur, juxta illud Sapientis : Infandorum idolorum cultura, omnis mali causa est, et principium et finis ; tradidit illos Deus, non effective, sed permissive, gratiam suam justissime subtrahendo, in desideria cordis eorum, id est in inordinatos appetitus et concupiscentias carnis, videlicet, in immunditiam luxuriæ, vel potius Sodomiticæ maculæ; ut contumeliis, hoc est actibus ipsi naturæ injuriosis, nocivis atque contrariis, afficiant corpora sua in semetipsis, hoc est, in eodem sexu atque supposito, committendo peccata contra naturam. Vel, in semetipsis, id est ad invicem : nam et qui fornicatur, peccat in corpus suum.
paras.en: [[1:24|Wherefore|Propter quod]], that is, because of the idolatry already mentioned, which becomes the origin of every sin, according to the word of the Wise Man: [[Wis 14:27|the worship of abominable idols is the cause, and the beginning and end of all evil|Infandorum idolorum cultura, omnis mali causa est, et principium et finis]]; [[1:24|God gave them up|tradidit illos Deus]], not by causing it but by permitting it, most justly withdrawing His grace, [[1:24|to the desires of their heart|in desideria cordis eorum]], that is, to disordered appetites and lusts of the flesh, namely [[1:24|unto uncleanness|in immunditiam]] of lechery, or rather of the Sodomitic stain; [[1:24|to dishonour|ut contumeliis]], that is, by acts injurious, harmful and contrary to nature itself, [[1:24|their own bodies among themselves|afficiant corpora sua in semetipsis]], that is, within the same sex and person [*suppositum*], committing sins against nature. Or, *among themselves*, that is, with one another: for [[1 Cor 6:18|he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body|qui fornicatur, peccat in corpus suum]].

paras.t: Qui commutaverunt veritatem Dei in mendacium, id est, divinitatem, honorem et gloriam, soli vero omnipotentique Deo adscribenda et exhibenda, transtulerunt ad deos falsos seu idola, et coluerunt et servierunt creaturæ, videlicet idolis suis, potius quam Creatori, qui est Deus benedictus in sæcula, amen. Ecce quanta perversitas. Hæc traditio impiorum in desideria cordis eorum, est gravissima pœna quam Deus in præsenti infligit. Et est pœna damni, cui in inferno correspondet carentia beatificæ fruitionis. Unde Dominus ait in Psalmo : Dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum ; ibunt in adinventionibus suis. Unum namque peccatum trahit ad aliud, idemque peccatum est peccatum et causa peccati, seu culpa et pœna culpæ. Nam homo unum committendo peccatum, meretur a Deo relinqui, atque in aliud prolabi. Et quanto aliquis se ipsum erigit altius, inaniusque extollit, tanto meretur profundius cadere. Maxime quoque, qui tam sapientes sunt in propriis oculis, merentur relinqui, in tantum ut vitia carnis incidant, quæ sunt præcipue bestialia atque turpissima. Unde jam subditur :
paras.en: [[1:25|Who changed the truth of God into a lie|Qui commutaverunt veritatem Dei in mendacium]], that is, the divinity, honour and glory to be ascribed and shown to the one true and almighty God alone they transferred to false gods or idols, [[1:25|and worshipped and served the creature|et coluerunt, et servierunt creaturæ]], namely their idols, [[1:25|rather than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen|potius quam Creatori, qui est Deus benedictus in sæcula, amen]] [Denis reads: who is God blessed for ever]. Behold how great a perversity! This giving up of the ungodly to the desires of their heart is the heaviest punishment that God inflicts in this present life. And it is a pain of loss [*pœna damni*, the punishment of being deprived of good], to which in hell there corresponds the want of the beatific enjoyment. Whence the Lord says in the Psalm: [[Ps 80:13|So I let them go according to the desires of their heart: they shall walk in their own inventions|Dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum ; ibunt in adinventionibus suis]]. For one sin draws to another, and the same sin is both sin and the cause of sin, or guilt and the punishment of guilt. For by committing one sin a man deserves to be forsaken by God and to slip into another. And the higher a man raises himself and the more emptily he exalts himself, the deeper he deserves to fall. Above all, those who are so wise in their own eyes[[Is 5:21||]] deserve to be forsaken, so far as to fall into the vices of the flesh, which are especially bestial and most foul. Hence it is now added:

paras.t: Propterea tradidit illos Deus in passiones ignominiæ, id est in innominabilia vitia carnis, quæ sunt peccata contra naturam. Ignominia enim dicitur, quasi sine nomine dignitatis, quoniam talia scelera non faciliter explicantur. Prosequitur tamen Apostolus species tanti facinoris. Nam feminæ eorum immutaverunt naturalem usum, in eum usum qui est contra naturam, hoc est, organo sui sexus, quod ordinatur ad conceptionem prolis, abusæ sunt, ita ut femina feminæ misceretur. Similiter autem et masculi, relicto naturali usu feminæ, id est legitima seu naturali commixtione ac copula cum muliere, exarserunt igne libidinis in desideriis suis turpissimis in invicem, scilicet, masculi in masculos turpitudinem operantes, polluendo se mutuo variis modis. Sed et si masculus feminæ commisceatur alio modo, loco, seu organo, quam natura concessit, contra naturam peccatur. Et mercedem, quam oportuit, erroris sui in semetipsis recipientes. Sic construenda et intelligenda est littera : Prædicti idololatræ ac Sodomitici, recipientes a Deo permissive, a se ipsis autem causaliter : recipientes, inquam, et sustinentes in semetipsis, id est in propria natura, mercedem sui erroris, id est retributionem seu præmium suæ idololatriæ, scilicet traditionem et lapsum in passiones ignominiæ : quam mercedem oportuit vel decuit eos recipere secundum dictamen ac ordinem divinæ justitiæ, qua vitia vitiis proportionaliter puniuntur. Unde quemadmodum jactantia propriæ sapientiæ meruit ut in idololatriam caderent, sic idololatria, propter gravissimam suam deformitatem, meruit ut innominabilia carnis peccata inciderent.
paras.en: [[1:26|For this cause, God delivered them up to shameful affections|Propterea tradidit illos Deus in passiones ignominiæ]], that is, to the unnameable vices of the flesh, which are sins against nature. For *ignominia* is so called as being without the name of dignity [*in-* + *nomen*], since such crimes are not easily spoken of. Yet the Apostle sets out the kinds of so great a crime. [[1:26|For their women have changed the natural use into that use which is against nature|Nam feminæ eorum immutaverunt naturalem usum, in eum usum qui est contra naturam]], that is, they abused the organ of their sex, which is ordered to the conception of offspring, so that woman was joined with woman. [[1:27|And, in like manner, the men also, leaving the natural use of the women|Similiter autem et masculi, relicto naturali usu feminæ]], that is, lawful or natural intercourse and union with a woman, [[1:27|have burned in their lusts, one towards another|exarserunt in desideriis suis in invicem]] with the fire of lust in their most shameful desires, namely, [[1:27|men with men, working that which is filthy|masculi in masculos turpitudinem operantes]], defiling one another in various ways. And even if a man is joined with a woman in another manner, place or organ than nature has granted, sin is committed against nature. [[1:27|and receiving in themselves the recompense which was due to their error|Et mercedem, quam oportuit, erroris sui in semetipsis recipientes]]. The text is to be construed and understood thus: The aforesaid idolaters and Sodomites, *receiving*, from God by permission, but from themselves as cause; receiving, I say, and undergoing *in themselves*, that is, in their own nature, *the recompense of their error*, that is, the requital or reward of their idolatry, namely being given up and falling into shameful affections: *which* recompense *was due*, or was fitting for them to receive according to the dictate and order of the divine justice, by which vices are punished by vices in due proportion. Hence, just as the boasting of their own wisdom deserved that they should fall into idolatry, so idolatry, because of its most grievous deformity, deserved that they should fall into the unnameable sins of the flesh.

paras.t: Et sicut non probaverunt, hoc est, non putaverunt nec opere ostenderunt, Deum habere in notitia actus humanos, id est, æstimaverunt Deum non cognoscere peccata hominum, dicentes illud Job : Deus excelsior cœlo est, nec nostra considerat, et circa cardines cœli perambulat; et illud Ezechielis, Dereliquit Dominus terram, et Dominus nos non videt; tradidit illos Deus in reprobum sensum, hoc est in intellectum perversum, privando eos lumine gratiæ ac veræ sapientiæ, quatenus, sicut circa divinum intellectum erraverunt, sic in suo intellectu punirentur. Tales sunt omnes qui divinam providentiam negant. De quibus ait Psalmista : Dixerunt, Non videbit Dominus, nec intelliget Deus Jacob; et Sophonias, Dicunt, Non faciet Dominus bene, et non faciet male. Contra quos Dominus loquitur per Amos prophetam : Cognovi multa scelera vestra, et fortia peccata vestra. Vel sic : Sicut non probaverunt, hoc est, non curaverunt, Deum habere in notitia, id est cognoscere Deum veraciter, tradidit illos in reprobum sensum, excæcando corda ipsorum permissive, ita quod eis convenit illud propheticum : Sapientes sunt ut faciant mala, bene autem facere nescierunt. Ut faciant ea quæ non conveniunt, hoc est, quæ Deo, rationi, atque Ecclesiæ contrariantur. Hæc dictio, Ut, non tenetur hoc loco causaliter, sed concomitanter. Non enim idcirco tradidit illos in reprobum sensum directe, ut faciant mala; sed operatio mali consecuta est traditionem, seu derelictionem ipsorum prædictam. Sicque frequenter in libro isto accipitur.
paras.en: [[1:28|And as they liked not|Et sicut non probaverunt]], that is, did not think nor show by their deeds, [[1:28|to have God in their knowledge|Deum habere in notitia]] human acts [Denis reads: that God has human acts in His knowledge], that is, they reckoned that God does not know the sins of men, saying that word of Job: [[Job 22:12|God is higher than heaven|Deus excelsior cœlo est]], [[Job 22:14|he doth not consider our things, and he walketh about the poles of heaven|nec nostra considerat, et circa cardines cœli perambulat]]; and that of Ezechiel, [[Ezech 9:9|The Lord hath forsaken the earth, and the Lord seeth not|Dereliquit Dominus terram, et Dominus nos non videt]]; [[1:28|God delivered them up to a reprobate sense|tradidit illos Deus in reprobum sensum]], that is, to a perverse understanding, depriving them of the light of grace and of true wisdom, so that as they erred about the divine understanding, they should be punished in their own understanding. Such are all who deny the divine providence. Of whom the Psalmist says: [[Ps 93:7|And they have said: The Lord shall not see: neither shall the God of Jacob understand|Dixerunt, Non videbit Dominus, nec intelliget Deus Jacob]]; and Sophonias, They say, [[Soph 1:12|The Lord will not do good, nor will he do evil|Non faciet Dominus bene, et non faciet male]]. Against whom the Lord speaks by the prophet Amos: [[Amos 5:12|I know your manifold crimes, and your grievous sins|Cognovi multa scelera vestra, et fortia peccata vestra]]. Or thus: *As they liked not*, that is, cared not, *to have God in their knowledge*, that is, to know God truly, He delivered them up to a reprobate sense, blinding their hearts by permission, so that that prophetic word fits them: [[Jer 4:22|they are wise to do evil, but to do good they have no knowledge|Sapientes sunt ut faciant mala, bene autem facere nescierunt]]. [[1:28|to do those things which are not convenient|ut faciant ea quæ non conveniunt]], that is, things contrary to God, to reason and to the Church. The word *ut* [*to*, *so that*] is not taken here causally but concomitantly. For He did not directly deliver them to a reprobate sense in order that they might do evil; but the doing of evil followed upon their being given up, or forsaken, as said. And so it is often taken in this book.

paras.t: Sic ergo tradidit illos Deus repletos omni iniquitate, hoc est omni peccato. Peccatum enim iniquitas est, id est contra justitiam, secundum Joannem. Præterea, ponit partes seu species iniquitatis : malitia, qua alter alteri damnum inferre conatur; fornicatione, hoc est illegitimo cum muliere concubitu; avaritia, hoc est inordinato appetitu temporalium rerum, nequitia, id est perversitate, seu temeritate nefaria, plenos invidia, quæ est tristitia de bono alterius; homicidiis, contentione, dolo; malignitate, hoc est voluntate igne malitiæ inflammata; susurrones, hoc est discordiæ seminatores : contra quos Moyses præcipit, Non eris susurro in populo; et Ecclesiasticus ait : Susurro et bilinguis maledictus; multos enim turbavit pacem habentes. Detractores, hoc est aliorum famam denigrantes, de eorum defectibus inordinate loquendo, vel falsa imponendo. Deo odibiles quantum ad culpam. Odio enim Deo sunt impius, et impietas ejus. Unde Ecclesiastes ait : Si mordeat serpens in silentio, nihil minus eo habet qui occulte detrahit. Agendum est ergo quod ait vir sanctus : Detrahentem secreto proximo suo, hunc persequebar. Contumeliosos, id est verbis vel actibus injuriantes. Quod valde iniquum est, juxta illud : Homo assuetus in verbis improperii, omnibus diebus vitæ suæ non dirigetur. Superbos, appetendo honores; elatos, nolendo habere æqualem aut superiorem; inventores malorum, excogitando novos errores, aut culpas; parentibus non obedientes; insipientes, male sentiendo de rebus divinis; incompositos moribus, sine affectione, id est tepidos, carentes zelo justitiæ et caritatis fervore, absque fœdere, id est observatione pacti, societatis et amicitiæ. Unde scriptum est : Qui dissolvit pactum, numquid effugiet? Sine misericordia, id est crudeles. Viscera namque impiorum crudelia. In talibus adimpletur quod Jacobus ait : Judicium sine misericordia fiet ei qui non fecerit misericordiam.
paras.en: So then God delivered them up, [[1:29|Being filled with all iniquity|repletos omni iniquitate]], that is, with every sin. For [[1 John 3:4|sin is iniquity|Peccatum enim iniquitas est]], that is, against justice, according to John. Further, he sets down the parts or kinds of iniquity: [[1:29|malice|malitia]], by which one tries to do another harm; [[1:29|fornication|fornicatione]], that is, unlawful lying with a woman; [[1:29|avarice|avaritia]], that is, disordered craving for temporal things; [[1:29|wickedness|nequitia]], that is, perversity, or wicked rashness; [[1:29|full of envy|plenos invidia]], which is sorrow at another's good; [[1:29|murder, contention, deceit|homicidio, contentione, dolo]]; [[1:29|malignity|malignitate]], that is, a will inflamed with the fire of malice; [[1:29|whisperers|susurrones]], that is, sowers of discord: against whom Moses commands, [[Lev 19:16|Thou shalt not be a detractor nor a whisperer among the people|Non eris susurro in populo]]; and Ecclesiasticus says: [[Ecclus 28:15|The whisperer and the double tongue is accursed: for he hath troubled many that were at peace|Susurro et bilinguis maledictus; multos enim turbavit pacem habentes]]. [[1:30|Detractors|Detractores]], that is, blackening the good name of others by speaking inordinately of their faults or by imputing falsehoods. [[1:30|hateful to God|Deo odibiles]] as regards guilt. For [[Wis 14:9|to God the wicked and his wickedness are hateful alike|Odio enim Deo sunt impius, et impietas ejus]]. Whence Ecclesiastes says: [[Eccles 10:11|If a serpent bite in silence, he is nothing better that backbiteth secretly|Si mordeat serpens in silentio, nihil minus eo habet qui occulte detrahit]]. We must do, then, what the holy man says: [[Ps 100:5|The man that in private detracted his neighbour, him did I persecute|Detrahentem secreto proximo suo, hunc persequebar]]. [[1:30|contumelious|contumeliosos]], that is, wronging others by words or deeds; which is very wicked, according to that word: [[Ecclus 23:20|The man that is accustomed to opprobrious words, will never be corrected all the days of his life|Homo assuetus in verbis improperii, omnibus diebus vitæ suæ non dirigetur]]. [[1:30|proud|superbos]], by seeking honours; [[1:30|haughty|elatos]], by being unwilling to have an equal or a superior; [[1:30|inventors of evil things|inventores malorum]], by devising new errors or faults; [[1:30|disobedient to parents|parentibus non obedientes]]; [[1:31|Foolish|insipientes]], by thinking wrongly of divine things; [[1:31|dissolute|incompositos]] in their manners; [[1:31|without affection|sine affectione]], that is, lukewarm, lacking zeal for justice and the fervour of charity; [[1:31|without fidelity|absque fœdere]], that is, without keeping of covenant, fellowship and friendship. Whence it is written: [[Ezech 17:15|shall he that hath done thus prosper, or be saved? and shall he escape that hath broken the covenant?|Qui dissolvit pactum, numquid effugiet]]? [[1:31|without mercy|sine misericordia]], that is, cruel. For [[Prov 12:10|the bowels of the wicked are cruel|Viscera namque impiorum crudelia]]. In such is fulfilled what James says: [[Jas 2:13|judgment without mercy to him that hath not done mercy|Judicium sine misericordia fiet ei qui non fecerit misericordiam]].

paras.t: Qui quum justitiam Dei, hoc est justum Deum, cognovissent, non tamen intellexerunt, hoc scilicet, quoniam qui talia agunt, digni sunt morte æterna; et non solum qui ea faciunt sunt digni morte, sed etiam qui consentiunt facientibus, ut nullus excusetur.
paras.en: [[1:32|Who, having known the justice of God|Qui cum justitiam Dei cognovissent]], that is, the just God, [[1:32|did not understand|non intellexerunt]] this, namely, [[1:32|that they who do such things, are worthy of death|quoniam qui talia agunt, digni sunt morte]] eternal; [[1:32|and not only they that do them|et non solum qui ea faciunt]] are worthy of death, [[1:32|but they also that consent to them that do them|sed etiam qui consentiunt facientibus]], so that none may be excused.

8.title: EXPLANATIO CAPITULI OCTAVI : NIHIL ERGO NUNC DAMNATIONIS EST, ETC.
8.title_en: Explanation of the eighth chapter: There is now therefore no condemnation, etc.

paras.t: DECLARATA in præcedenti capitulo cessatione legis Mosaicæ, jam docet Christo et evangelicæ legi jugiter inhærendum, et ait : Nihil ergo nunc, scilicet tempore gratiæ, damnationis, id est obligationis ad pœnam gehennæ, est his qui sunt in Christo Jesu per fidem et caritatem : quibus ipse loquitur, Manete in me, et ego in vobis ; qui non secundum carnem ambulant, id est, carnis desideriis non acquiescunt, neque carnaliter vivunt, sed carnem cum vitiis et concupiscentiis crucifigunt. In fonte namque Baptismatis dimissa sunt eis peccata universa. Si autem postea non peccaverunt, manendo in Christo proferunt fructum multum, et ita non tantum pro vitiis satisfaciunt, sed insuper gloriam ampliorem merentur. Lex enim spiritus vitæ, id est lex evangelica : quæ nominatur lex spiritus, quia a Spiritu Sancto est data, Christianorumque cordibus ab ipso impressa; dicitur quoque lex vitæ, quoniam mentem vivificat, per gratiam quam sacramenta novæ legis distribuunt; in Christo Jesu, id est per Christum, liberavit me a lege peccati et mortis, id est a consensu, consuetudine, et actu culpæ ac pœnæ pro culpa infligendæ. Potest quoque per legem peccati, lex scripta intelligi, eo quod ex occasione auxerit culpam ac pœnam, quemadmodum in superioribus ubertim expositum est.
paras.en: Having in the preceding chapter set forth the ceasing of the Mosaic law, he now teaches that we must cleave constantly to Christ and to the law of the Gospel, and says: [[8:1|There is now therefore|Nihil ergo nunc]], that is, in the time of grace, [[8:1|no condemnation|damnationis]], that is, no liability to the punishment of hell, [[8:1|to them that are in Christ Jesus|est his qui sunt in Christo Jesu]] by faith and charity: to whom He Himself says, [[John 15:4|Abide in me: and I in you|Manete in me, et ego in vobis]]; [[8:1|who walk not according to the flesh|qui non secundum carnem ambulant]], that is, who do not yield to the desires of the flesh nor live carnally, but crucify the flesh with its vices and concupiscences[[Gal 5:24||]]. For in the font of Baptism all their sins were forgiven them. And if afterwards they have not sinned, by abiding in Christ they bring forth much fruit[[John 15:5||]], and so not only make satisfaction for their faults, but moreover merit greater glory. [[8:2|For the law of the spirit of life|Lex enim spiritus vitæ]], that is, the law of the Gospel: which is called the law of the spirit because it was given by the Holy Ghost and imprinted by Him on the hearts of Christians; and it is called the law of life because it quickens the mind through the grace which the sacraments of the new law dispense; [[8:2|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, through Christ, [[8:2|hath delivered me from the law of sin and of death|liberavit me a lege peccati et mortis]], that is, from the consent, the habit and the act of guilt, and from the punishment to be inflicted for guilt. By the law of sin may also be understood the written law, in that it occasionally increased guilt and punishment, as was set forth at length above[[Rom 7:8||]].

paras.t: Proinde declarat Apostolus, quomodo lex Christi, quæ est lex spiritus vitæ, liberet a lege peccati et mortis. Nam quod impossibile erat legi scriptæ et sacramentis ipsius, non continentibus nec conferentibus gratiam, in quo infirmabatur, id est, in qua impossibilitate atque inefficacia, infirma et ad salvandum impotens erat lex ipsa, per carnem, id est per observantias et justificationes carnales, quæ non purificant animam. Sacramenta enim legalia corporaliter tantum mundabant, quasdam inhabilitates seu irregularitates ab exteriori inductas, et ab ingressu templi atque similibus impedientes, tollendo. Vel, Per carnem, id est per fomitem carnis, quem lex occasionaliter incitavit, non directe diminuit. Deus Pater Filium suum mittens in mundum per incarnationis mysterium, non per localem descensum, in similitudinem carnis peccati, id est in corpore mortali atque passibili : quod licet fuerit veraciter veraque caro, non tamen veraciter erat caro peccati, sed similitudinarie. Per pœnas enim quas pertulit, similis erat carni peccatrici. Venit itaque Christus in veritate carnis, non autem in veritate carnis peccati, sed in similitudine ejus.
paras.en: Next the Apostle shows how the law of Christ, which is the law of the spirit of life, delivers from the law of sin and of death. [[8:3|For what the law could not do|Nam quod impossibile erat legi]], the written law and its sacraments, which neither contained nor conferred grace, [[8:3|in that it was weak|in quo infirmabatur]], that is, in which impossibility and inefficacy the law itself was weak and powerless to save, [[8:3|through the flesh|per carnem]], that is, through carnal observances and justifications, which do not purify the soul. For the legal sacraments cleansed only bodily, by removing certain disabilities or irregularities contracted from without, which barred from entering the temple and the like. Or, through the flesh, that is, through the fomes of the flesh [the inclination to sin left in fallen nature], which the law occasionally stirred up and did not directly lessen. [[8:3|God, sending his own Son|Deus Pater Filium suum mittens]] (God the Father) into the world through the mystery of the Incarnation, not by a descent in place, [[8:3|in the likeness of sinful flesh|in similitudinem carnis peccati]], that is, in a mortal and passible body: which, though it was truly and really flesh, was not truly flesh of sin, but only by likeness. For through the penalties which He bore He was like to sinful flesh. Christ therefore came in the reality of flesh, but not in the reality of sinful flesh, only in its likeness.

paras.t: Et de peccato damnavit peccatum : id est, Pater mittens sic Filium, damnavit, id est, delevit, destruxit, dimisit peccatum, tam originale quam actuale, de peccato, id est per peccatum factum in carne Christi, non a Christo, sed a diabolo ejusque ministris qui Christum occiderunt. Per hoc enim quod Christus injuste occisus est, suggerente diabolo, amisit diabolus jus quod habebat in nobis, et ita mors Christo inique illata, omne peccatum delevit. Vel : Damnavit peccatum actuale, nascens de peccato, id est fomite peccati ; vel, Peccatum de peccato, id est fomitem peccati, procedentem de peccato originali Adæ. Vel sic, et melius, secundum Ambrosium : De peccato, id est de se ipso, prout factus est hostia pro peccato nostro, damnavit, id est delevit, peccatum mundi quodcumque, in carne, id est in corporis sui passione. Ipse enim portavit peccata nostra in corpore suo super lignum. Juxta hunc sensum sacrificia legis pro peccatis oblata, dicebantur peccata, secundum quod de sacerdotibus veteris Testamenti Dominus ait per Osee : Peccata populi mei comedent. Sic quoque aquam cum periculo vitæ allatam David, sanguinem appellavit, dicens : Absit a me, ut sanguinem virorum istorum bibam.
paras.en: [[8:3|and of sin, hath condemned sin|et de peccato, damnavit peccatum]]: that is, the Father, sending the Son thus, condemned, that is, blotted out, destroyed, remitted sin, original as well as actual, of sin, that is, by the sin committed [[8:3|in the flesh|in carne]] of Christ, not by Christ, but by the devil and his ministers who slew Christ. For because Christ was unjustly slain at the devil's prompting, the devil lost the right he had over us, and so the death wickedly inflicted on Christ blotted out all sin. Or: He condemned actual sin, springing of sin, that is, of the fomes of sin; or, sin of sin, that is, the fomes of sin proceeding from the original sin of Adam. Or thus, and better, according to Ambrose: Of sin, that is, of Himself, inasmuch as He was made a victim for our sin, He condemned, that is, blotted out, every sin of the world, in the flesh, that is, in the passion of His body. For [[1 Pet 2:24|Who his own self bore our sins in his body upon the tree|Ipse … portavit … super lignum]]. In this sense the sacrifices of the law offered for sins were called sins, as the Lord says through Osee of the priests of the Old Testament: [[Osee 4:8|They shall eat the sins of my people|Peccata populi mei comedent]] [Denis's word order differs slightly from the Vulgate]. So too David called the water brought at peril of life blood, saying: [[1 Par 11:19|God forbid that I should do this in the sight of my God, and should drink the blood of these men|Absit a me, ut sanguinem virorum istorum bibam]].

paras.t: Hæc itaque fecit Deus, ut justificatio legis, id est in lege promissa, non autem per legem exhibita : lex enim gratiam justificantem spopondit, non contulit: impleretur in nobis, qui in Baptismo aliisque sacramentis gratiam justificantem in lege præfiguratam ac prænuntiatam recipimus, qui non secundum carnem ambulamus, sed secundum spiritum, id est, non carnaliter, sed spiritualiter in hujus vitæ exsilio conversamur, tendentes ac properantes ad patriam per opera virtuosa. De hac legis promissione aiebat Apostolus loquens de Judæis : Et nos vobis annuntiamus eam quæ ad patres nostros facta est repromissio, quoniam hanc Deus implevit filiis nostris. Hinc etiam Petrus in sua Canonica : De qua salute exquisierunt atque scrutati sunt Prophetæ, qui de futura in vobis gratia prophetaverunt : quibus revelatum est quia non sibi ipsis, vobis autem ministraverunt ea quæ nunc nuntiata sunt vobis.
paras.en: These things, then, God did [[8:4|That the justification of the law|ut justificatio legis]], that is, promised in the law, but not bestowed through the law (for the law promised justifying grace but did not confer it), [[8:4|might be fulfilled in us|impleretur in nobis]], who in Baptism and the other sacraments receive the justifying grace prefigured and foretold in the law, [[8:4|who walk not according to the flesh, but according to the spirit|qui non secundum carnem ambulamus, sed secundum spiritum]], that is, who live in the exile of this life not carnally but spiritually, tending and hastening to the fatherland by virtuous works. Of this promise of the law the Apostle said, speaking of the Jews: [[Acts 13:32|And we declare unto you that the promise which was made|Et nos vobis annuntiamus eam quæ ad patres nostros facta est]], [[Acts 13:33|This same God hath fulfilled to our children|quoniam hanc Deus implevit filiis nostris]]. Hence also Peter in his Canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 1:10|Of which salvation the prophets have inquired and diligently searched, who prophesied of the grace to come in you|De qua salute exquisierunt atque scrutati sunt Prophetæ, qui de futura in vobis]] [[1 Pet 1:12|To whom it was revealed that, not to themselves but to you, they ministered those things which are now declared to you|quibus revelatum est quia non sibi ipsis, vobis autem ministraverunt ea quæ nunc nuntiata sunt vobis]].

paras.t: Pro intellectu loci hujus intricati atque difficilis advertendum, quod nemo unquam salvatus est nisi per fidem et gratiam Christi. Ipse enim est caput omnium electorum ; membra autem necesse est capiti counire, ut vitam participent. Propter quod Petrus disserebat : Nec enim aliud nomen sub cœlo datum est hominibus, in quo oporteat nos salvos fieri. Passio namque Christi hoc fecit futura, quod facit impleta.
paras.en: For the understanding of this intricate and difficult passage, note that no one was ever saved except through faith in Christ and His grace. For He is the head of all the elect[[Eph 1:22||]]; and the members must be united to the head in order to share its life. Wherefore Peter declared: [[Acts 4:12|For there is no other name under heaven given to men, whereby we must be saved|Nec enim aliud nomen sub cœlo datum est hominibus, in quo oporteat nos salvos fieri]]. For the passion of Christ, while yet to come, did the same as it does now accomplished.

paras.t: Porro, hæc salus aliter applicatur hominibus post Christi passionem, et aliter ante. Tunc enim applicabatur per fidem formatam, nunc vero applicatur etiam per sacramenta gratiæ contentiva, effectiva et causativa. Potest autem aliquid movere vel agere, antequam sit in effectu, videlicet secundum quod est in apprehensione animæ, et dispositione causæ efficientis, quemadmodum finis movet agentem. Ad hoc autem quod aliquid agat et moveat in genere causæ efficientis, oportet ut sit, et effectum præcedat, eo quod causa effectiva non sit suo effectu posterior. Sacramenta ergo veteris legis et fides Christi venturi, habere non poterant quemlibet effectum dominicæ passionis, quem nunc habent sacramenta ac fides evangelicæ legis, quæ operantur virtute passionis dominicæ jam impletæ. Et ideo gratiam operantur, et a reatu originalis peccati absolvunt : quorum nullum sacramenta legis facere poterant. Unde omnes patres pro tunc descenderunt in limbum inferni. Nam licet per fidem et gratiam Dei, virtute passionis Christi et merito ejus futuro, absolverentur a pœna et culpa actualium peccatorum, non tamen a reatu originalis peccati.
paras.en: Now this salvation is applied to men in one way after Christ's passion and in another before it. Then it was applied through formed faith [that is, faith informed by charity]; now it is applied also through sacraments which contain, effect and cause grace. A thing can move or act before it exists in fact, namely inasmuch as it is in the apprehension of the mind and in the intention of the efficient cause, as the end moves the agent. But for a thing to act and move in the order of efficient cause, it must exist and precede the effect, since an efficient cause is not later than its effect. The sacraments of the old law, therefore, and faith in Christ to come, could not have every effect of the Lord's passion which the sacraments and faith of the Gospel law now have, which work by the power of the Lord's passion already accomplished. And so these work grace and absolve from the guilt of original sin, neither of which the sacraments of the law could do. Hence all the fathers of that time went down into the limbo of hell. For although through faith and the grace of God, by the power of Christ's passion and His merit yet to come, they were absolved from the punishment and guilt of actual sins, they were not absolved from the guilt of original sin.

paras.t: Ex quo innotescit, quod passio Christi fortius agit impleta, quam egit implenda. Quemadmodum enim sacramenta novæ legis, sunt causæ instrumentales nostræ salutis et gratiæ, quoniam agunt virtute et merito passionis dominicæ, suntque vasa medicinalia spiritualium unguentorum contentiva, animarum languores curantia ; sic humanitas seu passio Christi, est causa instrumentalis, effectiva et meritoria nostræ salutis et gratiæ. Utrumque vero est instrumentum divinitatis Christi. Divinitas namque est causa efficiens principalis, quæ agit per humanitatem assumptam sicut per instrumentum conjunctum, per sacramenta vero, sicut per instrumenta separata : quemadmodum medicus est causa sanitatis efficiens principalis, manus autem est sicut causa instrumentalis conjuncta, ignis vero quo medicina paratur, est causa instrumentalis separata. Causa autem instrumentalis quum est in effectu, vel quum causa ejus principalis jam est, fortius operatur quam ante. Hinc ergo ait Apostolus, quod Deus misit Filium suum, de peccato damnans peccatum, ut justificatio legis impleretur in nobis : quod impossibile erat legi, justificare non valenti, in quo lex infirmabatur, seu debilis erat. Et hoc modo construenda est littera.
paras.en: From this it appears that the passion of Christ acts more powerfully now accomplished than it acted when yet to be accomplished. For as the sacraments of the new law are instrumental causes of our salvation and grace, since they act by the power and merit of the Lord's passion, and are medicinal vessels containing spiritual ointments that heal the sicknesses of souls; so the humanity or passion of Christ is the instrumental, effective and meritorious cause of our salvation and grace. Both are instruments of the Godhead of Christ. For the Godhead is the principal efficient cause, acting through the assumed humanity as through a conjoined instrument, and through the sacraments as through separate instruments: as the physician is the principal efficient cause of health, the hand as a conjoined instrumental cause, and the fire with which the medicine is prepared a separate instrumental cause. And an instrumental cause, when it exists in fact, or when its principal cause already exists, works more powerfully than before. Hence the Apostle says that God sent His Son, condemning sin of sin, that the justification of the law might be fulfilled in us: which was impossible to the law, which could not justify, in which the law was weak or feeble. And in this way the text is to be construed.

paras.t: Quod autem justificatio legis non nisi in spiritualibus impleatur hominibus, liquet. Qui enim secundum carnem sunt, id est, qui carnaliter vivunt : qui utique attendunt se ipsos secundum esse suum carnale ac sensitivum, non secundum esse spirituale ac intellectivum ; quæ carnis sunt, sapiunt, id est, carnalia gustant, sensibilia ac temporalia cum sensualitatis sapore attendunt. Qui vero secundum spiritum, id est spiritualiter conversantes, et esse suum supremum, in quo Trinitatis imago relucet, pensantes, quæ sunt spiritus sentiunt, id est, spiritualia atque divina saporose intelligunt, delectabiliter pensant, sollicite implent, in talibus jugiter occupantur.
paras.en: That the justification of the law is fulfilled only in spiritual men is plain. [[8:5|For they that are according to the flesh|Qui enim secundum carnem sunt]], that is, who live carnally, who regard themselves according to their carnal and sensitive being, not according to their spiritual and intellectual being, [[8:5|mind the things that are of the flesh|quæ carnis sunt, sapiunt]], that is, relish carnal things, attend to sensible and temporal things with the savour of sensuality [the Latin *sapiunt*, “mind”, is akin to *sapor*, taste]. [[8:5|but they that are according to the spirit|Qui vero secundum spiritum]], that is, those who live spiritually and ponder their highest being, in which the image of the Trinity shines, [[8:5|mind the things that are of the spirit|quæ sunt spiritus, sentiunt]], that is, understand spiritual and divine things with relish, ponder them with delight, carry them out with care, and are constantly occupied in them.

paras.t: Nam prudentia carnis, id est carnalis ac sæcularis prudentia, mors est, id est mortale peccatum, inferens mortem culpæ in via, mortemque pœnæ in gehenna. Dicitur autem prudentia carnis hoc loco, per quam homo sibi in bonis carnalibus ac mundanis finem constituit, et ad talis finis adeptionem opera sua caute disponit. Hæc prudentia, non est vera prudentia, sed appellatur prudentia, propter apparentem similitudinem quam habet cum vera prudentia. Unde ait Salvator : Filii hujus sæculi prudentiores filiis lucis in generatione sua sunt ; et Jacobus, Non est ista sapientia (id est prudentia) a Deo, sed terrena, animalis et diabolica. Prudentia autem spiritus, id est vera ac spiritualis prudentia, quæ opera hominis convenienter disponit in ordine ad ultimum finem, est vita et pax, id est causa vitæ et pacis, in præsenti inchoative, in futuro perfecte. Nunc enim efficit in nobis vitam pacemque gratiæ, in patria vero meretur, vel potius adipiscitur, pacem et vitam gloriæ. Non distinguit Apostolus jam inter prudentiam et sapientiam. Proprie enim ad sapientiam spectat spiritualia sapere. De hac ergo spirituali prudentia, intelligendum est illud Jacobi : Quæ desursum est sapientia, primum quidem pudica est, deinde pacifica, modesta, suasibilis, bonis consentiens. Sciendum quoque quod pax directe ac proprie, est caritatis effectus, juxta illud in Psalmo : Pax multa diligentibus legem tuam. Est etiam pax effectus justitiæ, tanquam removentis impedimenta pacis. Propter quod per Isaiam dicitur : Erit opus justitiæ pax. Nunc vero dicitur pax esse effectus prudentiæ, tanquam dirigentis affectus nostros in viam pacis.
paras.en: [[8:6|For the wisdom of the flesh|Nam prudentia carnis]] [the Latin has *prudentia*, prudence], that is, carnal and worldly prudence, [[8:6|is death|mors est]], that is, mortal sin, bringing the death of guilt on the way and the death of punishment in hell. Here prudence of the flesh means that by which a man sets his end in carnal and worldly goods and cunningly orders his works to the attaining of such an end. This is not true prudence, but is called prudence because of its apparent likeness to true prudence. Hence the Saviour says: [[Luke 16:8|the children of this world are wiser in their generation than the children of light|Filii hujus sæculi prudentiores filiis lucis in generatione sua sunt]]; and James: [[Jas 3:15|For this is not wisdom|Non est ista sapientia]] (that is, prudence) [[Jas 3:15|descending from above: but earthly, sensual, devilish|a Deo, sed terrena, animalis et diabolica]]. [[8:6|but the wisdom of the spirit|Prudentia autem spiritus]], that is, true and spiritual prudence, which fitly orders a man's works to the last end, is [[8:6|life and peace|vita et pax]], that is, the cause of life and peace, begun in the present, perfect in the future. For now it works in us the life and peace of grace, and in the fatherland it merits, or rather attains, the peace and life of glory. The Apostle here does not distinguish between prudence and wisdom, though properly it belongs to wisdom to savour spiritual things. Of this spiritual prudence, then, is to be understood that saying of James: [[Jas 3:17|But the wisdom that is from above, first indeed is chaste, then peaceable, modest, easy to be persuaded, consenting to the good|Quæ desursum est sapientia, primum quidem pudica est, deinde pacifica, modesta, suasibilis, bonis consentiens]]. Know too that peace is directly and properly the effect of charity, according to the Psalm: [[Ps 118:165|Much peace have they that love thy law|Pax multa diligentibus legem tuam]]. Peace is also the effect of justice, as removing the hindrances of peace; wherefore it is said through Isaias: [[Is 32:17|And the work of justice shall be peace|Erit opus justitiæ pax]]. Here peace is said to be the effect of prudence, as directing our affections into the way of peace.

paras.t: Quoniam sapientia carnis inimica est Deo, id est divinæ voluntati atque sapientiæ veræ contraria. Ecce nunc loco prudentiæ ponit sapientiam : ex quo certum est, quod inter sapientiam et prudentiam non distinguit. Legi enim Dei non est subjecta sapientia ista carnalis, mundana ac vana, quia nec credit nec agit quæ lex divina tradit esse credenda sive agenda. Propter quod ait Salvator : Confiteor tibi, Pater, quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis ; et Jeremias, Sapientes sunt ut faciant mala, bene autem facere nescierunt. Nec enim potest divinæ legi esse subjecta sapientia ista. Unum namque oppositorum non subjicitur alteri, sed repugnat. Lex autem divina docet ultimum finem esse constituendum in Deo, hæc vero in bonis carnalibus. Qui autem in carne sunt, id est, carnaliter vivunt, atque in sensibilibus bonis finaliter sistunt, Deo placere non possunt, in quantum hujusmodi. Possunt tamen converti, et Deo reconciliari. Huic dicto consonat illud Salvatoris : Nemo potest duobus dominis servire.
paras.en: [[8:7|Because the wisdom of the flesh is an enemy to God|Quoniam sapientia carnis inimica est Deo]], that is, contrary to the divine will and to true wisdom. See, he now puts wisdom in place of prudence; whence it is certain that he does not distinguish between them. [[8:7|For it is not subject to the law of God|Legi enim Dei non est subjecta]], this carnal, worldly and vain wisdom, because it neither believes nor does what the divine law teaches must be believed or done. Wherefore the Saviour says: [[Luke 10:21|I confess to thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hidden these things from the wise and prudent and hast revealed them to little ones|Confiteor tibi, Pater, quia abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis]]; and Jeremias: [[Jer 4:22|they are wise to do evil, but to do good|Sapientes sunt ut faciant mala, bene autem facere nescierunt]]. [[8:7|neither can it be|Nec enim potest]] subject to the divine law, this wisdom. For one of two opposites is not subject to the other but resists it. The divine law teaches that the last end is to be placed in God, this wisdom places it in carnal goods. [[8:8|And they who are in the flesh|Qui autem in carne sunt]], that is, who live carnally and rest finally in sensible goods, [[8:8|cannot please God|Deo placere non possunt]], insofar as they are such. Yet they can be converted and reconciled to God. With this saying agrees that of the Saviour: [[Matt 6:24|No man can serve two masters|Nemo potest duobus dominis servire]].

paras.t: Vos autem, o veraciter Christifideles, in carne non estis, id est, in rebus ac vitiis carnis non detinemini, sed spiritualia atque divina exquiritis, conversationem habentes in cœlis, sed in spiritu, id est, in Spiritu Sancto estis, per caritatem et gratiam, et propter spiritualem regenerationem, qua estis ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto renati. Vel, Estis in spiritu vestro, id est secundum rationis judicium vivitis : juxta quod scriptum est, Redite, prævaricatores, ad cor. Si tamen Spiritus Dei, id est Spiritus Sanctus, habitat, id est manet, in vobis per gratiam gratum facientem : quemadmodum loquitur Christus, Ego rogabo Patrem, et alium Paracletum dabit vobis, ut maneat vobiscum in æternum. Rursusque ait : Spiritus Sanctus apud vos manebit, et in vobis erit. Si quis autem Spiritum Christi non habet, id est, cujus anima non habitatur a Spiritu Sancto : qui est Spiritus Christi, quia ab ipso procedit, ab eoque datur ac mittitur, sicut ipse protestatur. Quum venerit Paracletus, quem ego mittam vobis a Patre : et iterum, Ille de meo accipiet. Et ad hoc designandum, insufflavit in discipulos suos, et dixit : Accipite Spiritum Sanctum. Quis autem habet Spiritum Sanctum, nisi quietus et humilis, simplex et justus? Scriptum est enim : Super quem requiescet Spiritus meus, nisi super quietum et humilem? Et iterum : Spiritus Sanctus disciplinæ effugiet fictum, et auferet se a cogitationibus quæ sunt sine intellectu. Hic non est ejus, id est, ad membra Christi non pertinet, secundum præsentem justitiam et merito, quamvis interdum pertineat secundum prædestinationem æternam ac numero, sicut et Paulus quum Stephanum lapidavit.
paras.en: [[8:9|But you are not in the flesh|Vos autem in carne non estis]], O truly faithful of Christ, that is, you are not held fast in the things and vices of the flesh, but seek spiritual and divine things, having your conversation in heaven[[Phil 3:20||]], [[8:9|but the spirit|sed in spiritu]], that is, you are in the Holy Ghost, by charity and grace, and by the spiritual regeneration whereby you are born again of water and the Holy Ghost[[John 3:5||]]. Or, you are in your own spirit, that is, you live according to the judgement of reason, as it is written: [[Is 46:8|return, ye transgressors, to the heart|Redite, prævaricatores, ad cor]]. [[8:9|if so be that the Spirit of God dwell in you|Si tamen Spiritus Dei habitat in vobis]], that is, the Holy Ghost abides in you through sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes one pleasing to God]: as Christ says, [[John 14:16|And I will ask the Father: and he shall give you another Paraclete, that he may abide with you for ever|Ego rogabo Patrem, et alium Paracletum dabit vobis, ut maneat vobiscum in æternum]]. And again He says: [[John 14:17|he shall abide with you and shall be in you|apud vos manebit, et in vobis erit]] [Denis supplies “the Holy Ghost” as subject]. [[8:9|Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ|Si quis autem Spiritum Christi non habet]], that is, whose soul is not indwelt by the Holy Ghost, who is the Spirit of Christ because He proceeds from Him and is given and sent by Him, as He Himself declares: [[John 15:26|But when the Paraclete cometh, whom I will send you from the Father|Quum venerit Paracletus, quem ego mittam vobis a Patre]] [the margin gives John xv, 26]; and again: [[John 16:14|he shall receive of mine|Ille de meo accipiet]]. And to signify this He breathed on His disciples and said: [[John 20:22|Receive ye the Holy Ghost|Accipite Spiritum Sanctum]]. But who has the Holy Ghost save the quiet and humble, the simple and just? For it is written: Upon whom shall my Spirit rest, but upon the quiet and the humble?[[Is 66:2||]] [the Vulgate reads differently: “to whom shall I have respect, but to him that is poor and little”]. And again: [[Wis 1:5|For the Holy Spirit of discipline will flee from the deceitful, and will withdraw himself from thoughts that are without understanding|Spiritus Sanctus disciplinæ effugiet fictum, et auferet se a cogitationibus quæ sunt sine intellectu]]. [[8:9|he is none of his|Hic non est ejus]], that is, he does not belong to the members of Christ according to present justice and by merit, though at times he belongs to them according to eternal predestination and in number, as Paul did when he stoned Stephen[[Acts 7:57||]].

paras.t: Deinde pandit Apostolus, quid utilitatis consequantur fideles ex inhabitatione Spiritus Sancti. Si autem Christus in vobis est, per fidem et caritatem : sicut et alibi legitur, Christum per fidem habitare in cordibus vestris; et Salvator ipse, Ego, inquit, vobiscum sum cunctis diebus ; corpus quidem mortuum est propter peccatum, id est, caro vestra mortalis ac fragilis, necessitati moriendi subjecta est propter originale peccatum, spiritus vero, id est anima vestra, vivit per gratiam, propter justificationem sibi a Christo collatam, id est per hoc quod peccata ei dimissa sunt, quæ spiritum vulnerabant. Vel, Propter justificationem, id est per justitiæ exercitationem. Bona enim operatio, vita est animæ. Hinc ait Salvator : Ego veni ut vitam habeant, et abundantius habeant.
paras.en: Then the Apostle shows what benefit the faithful gain from the indwelling of the Holy Ghost. [[8:10|And if Christ be in you|Si autem Christus in vobis est]] by faith and charity, as is read elsewhere, [[Eph 3:17|That Christ may dwell by faith in your hearts|Christum per fidem habitare in cordibus vestris]]; and the Saviour Himself says, [[Matt 28:20|I am with you all days|Ego … vobiscum sum … diebus]]; [[8:10|the body indeed is dead, because of sin|corpus quidem mortuum est propter peccatum]], that is, your mortal and frail flesh is subject to the necessity of dying because of original sin, [[8:10|but the spirit liveth|spiritus vero vivit]], that is, your soul lives by grace, [[8:10|because of justification|propter justificationem]] conferred on it by Christ, that is, because the sins which wounded the spirit have been forgiven it. Or, because of justification, that is, through the exercise of justice; for good works are the life of the soul. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 10:10|I am come that they may have life and may have it more abundantly|Ego veni ut vitam habeant, et abundantius habeant]].

paras.t: Quod si Spiritus ejus, id est Spiritus Dei Patris, qui suscitavit Jesum Christum a mortuis, habitat in vobis perseveranter usque in finem vitæ præsentis, ita ut in gratia decedatis; qui suscitavit Jesum Christum a mortuis, scilicet Deus Pater, vivificabit, id est, ad immortalem vitam resuscitabit, et mortalia corpora vestra in die novissimo : sicut Job apertissime profitetur : Credo quod Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum, et rursum circumdabor pelle mea. Per Isaiam quoque Dominus asserit : Vivent mortui tui, interfectique mei resurgent. Propter inhabitantem Spiritum ejus in vobis, id est virtute et gratia Spiritus Sancti; vel, propter benignitatem qua fecit Spiritum Sanctum habitare in mentibus vestris; vel, propter meritum quod consecuti estis ex inhabitatione et gratia Spiritus Sancti : imo, propter utrumque istorum simul, videlicet propter misericordiam Dei et opera vestra bona, suscitabuntur corpora vestra ad beatam et impassibilem vitam.
paras.en: [[8:11|And if the Spirit of him|Quod si Spiritus ejus]], that is, the Spirit of God the Father, [[8:11|that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you|qui suscitavit Jesum a mortuis, habitat in vobis]] perseveringly to the end of the present life, so that you depart in grace; [[8:11|he that raised up Jesus Christ, from the dead|qui suscitavit Jesum Christum a mortuis]], namely God the Father, [[8:11|shall quicken|vivificabit]], that is, shall raise to immortal life, [[8:11|also your mortal bodies|et mortalia corpora vestra]] on the last day: as Job most openly professes: [[Job 19:25|For I know that my Redeemer liveth, and in the last day I shall rise out of the earth|Credo quod Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum]] [[Job 19:26|And I shall be clothed again with my skin|et rursum circumdabor pelle mea]]. Through Isaias also the Lord declares: [[Is 26:19|Thy dead men shall live, my slain shall rise again|Vivent mortui tui, interfectique mei resurgent]]. [[8:11|because of his Spirit that dwelleth in you|propter inhabitantem Spiritum ejus in vobis]], that is, by the power and grace of the Holy Ghost; or, because of the kindness by which He made the Holy Ghost dwell in your minds; or, because of the merit you have gained from the indwelling and grace of the Holy Ghost: nay rather, for both of these together, namely for God's mercy and your good works, your bodies shall be raised to a blessed and impassible life.

paras.t: Ex prædictis infert Apostolus, quod fideles obtemperare tenentur rationi, non sensualitati : spiritui, non carni. Ergo, o fratres, debitores sumus non carni, ut secundum carnem vivamus : id est, quamvis aliquo modo obligemur carni, videlicet ut ei necessaria ministremus in victu atque vestitu, non tamen sic ei obligati sumus, ut ejus concupiscentiis acquiescamus, carnaliterque vivamus. Si enim secundum carnem vixeritis, moriemini, morte culpæ in hoc sæculo, et morte perpetua in inferno. Si autem spiritu, id est gratia Spiritus Sancti; vel, Spiritu, id est rationis vestræ judicio ; facta, id est opera, carnis mortificaveritis, id est, destruxeritis et abjeceritis tanquam venena : quemadmodum in Ecclesiastico præcipitur, Quasi a facie colubri fuge peccatum ; vivetis, vita caritatis et gratiæ in Ecclesia militanti, vita quoque fruitionis et gloriæ in Ecclesia triumphanti. Huic documento naturalis consonat ratio. Media namque disponenda sunt secundum exigentiam finis. Quum ergo caro sit animæ instrumentum, et ordinetur ad spiritum sicut ad finem, regenda est secundum exigentiam animæ seu spiritus, scilicet, ut animæ serviat, rationi obediat, illisque actibus occupetur per quæ spiritus tendit et redit ad Creatorem. Qui autem secundum carnem conversatur, pervertit hunc ordinem, dominam ancillæ subjiciens, finem medio postponens, et se ipsum bestiis viliorem ac deteriorem constituens.
paras.en: From the foregoing the Apostle infers that the faithful are bound to obey reason, not sensuality; the spirit, not the flesh. [[8:12|Therefore, brethren, we are debtors, not to the flesh to live according to the flesh|Ergo, o fratres, debitores sumus non carni, ut secundum carnem vivamus]]: that is, though we are in some way bound to the flesh, namely to supply it what it needs in food and clothing, yet we are not so bound to it as to yield to its concupiscences and live carnally. [[8:13|For if you live according to the flesh, you shall die|Si enim secundum carnem vixeritis, moriemini]], by the death of guilt in this world and by everlasting death in hell. [[8:13|but if by the Spirit|Si autem spiritu]], that is, by the grace of the Holy Ghost; or, by the spirit, that is, by the judgement of your reason, [[8:13|you mortify the deeds of the flesh|facta carnis mortificaveritis]], that is, the works, destroy them and cast them off as poisons: as is commanded in Ecclesiasticus, [[Ecclus 21:2|Flee from sins as from the face of a serpent|Quasi a facie colubri fuge peccatum]]; [[8:13|you shall live|vivetis]], the life of charity and grace in the Church militant, and the life of fruition and glory in the Church triumphant. Natural reason agrees with this teaching. For means must be ordered as the end requires. Since then the flesh is the instrument of the soul and is ordered to the spirit as to its end, it must be ruled as the soul or spirit requires: that it serve the soul, obey reason, and be occupied in those acts by which the spirit tends and returns to its Creator. But he who lives according to the flesh perverts this order, subjecting the mistress to the handmaid, putting the end after the means, and making himself viler and worse than the beasts.

paras.t: Quicumque enim Spiritu Dei aguntur, id est, a Spiritu Sancto reguntur, ejus instinctu ducuntur, ejus fervore impelluntur ad bona, hi sunt filii Dei, per gratiam adoptantem ac filialem amorem. Unde in Canonica Joannis scribitur : Videte qualem caritatem dedit nobis Deus Pater, ut filii Dei nominemur et simus. Quemadmodum autem Deus omnipotens movet ceteras creaturas ad proprias operationes, naturalemque finem, per quemdam universalem influxum seu generalem gubernationem (secundum quod Proclus auctor libri de Causis affirmat : Causa prima regit res omnes, præterquam quod commisceatur eis) ; sic rationalem creaturam movet ad finem supernaturalem per specialem gubernationem ac inspirationem, quæ providentia appellatur. Electos vero singulariter movet ac regit, providens eis non solum sufficienter, sed etiam efficaciter, de omnibus necessariis ad salutem, ita ut gratiam Dei suscipiant, ejusque inspirationi acquiescant. Idcirco dicuntur potius agi, quam regi vel moveri a Spiritu Sancto, ut magnitudo gratiæ insinuetur. Ad actum enim meritorium, non solum exigitur gratia habitualis, sed insuper necessaria est quædam actualis motio Spiritus Sancti voluntatem excitantis. Propter quod Propheta dicebat : Domine, omnia opera nostra operatus es in nobis. — Porro, quum motio ista sive influxus, actio et instinctus Spiritus Sancti, sit penitus supernaturalis, indiget anima supernaturalibus quibusdam habitibus, per quos aptetur ac disponatur ad hujus motionis facilem susceptionem. Hi vero habitus, sunt septem dona Spiritus Sancti, quæ sunt dispositiones habituales ac supernaturales, a Deo immediate per creationem infusæ, quibus redditur anima facile mobilis a Spiritu Sancto in ordine ad supernaturalem finem, quæ est vita æterna. Hæc dona a virtutibus realiter distinguuntur, easque in dignitate excedunt, theologicis demptis virtutibus. Per hæc dona dirigitur anima a Spiritu Sancto, ita ut audiat eum sicut magistrum. Unde ait Psalmista : Spiritus tuus bonus deducet me in terram rectam. — Qui itaque sic aguntur Spiritu Dei, hi sunt filii Dei. Quicumque autem in gratia est, habet hæc dona secundum aliquem gradum, et agitur a Spiritu Sancto quantum requirit status salutis, videlicet ad observantiam præceptorum.
paras.en: [[8:14|For whosoever are led by the Spirit of God|Quicumque enim Spiritu Dei aguntur]], that is, are ruled by the Holy Ghost, led by His prompting, driven to good things by His fervour, [[8:14|they are the sons of God|hi sunt filii Dei]], by adopting grace and filial love.
