paras.en: [[8:36|As it is written|Sicut scriptum est]][[Ps 43:22||]], in the person of the just or the martyrs suffering adversities, namely the pains already touched on: [[8:36|For thy sake|Quoniam propter te]], that is, for love of thee, and because we confess thee before men and will not depart from the way of thy justice; or, *for thy sake* as our end, that is, that we may gain thee, God, as our reward; [[8:36|we are put to death all the day long|mortificamur tota die]], that is, we are continually afflicted and brought to death by daily persecutions and adversities; or indeed because we mortify ourselves daily, by praying, mourning, abstaining, fighting against our own concupiscences, cheating our own will, and toiling in the other exercises of the virtues and the labours of penance; [[8:36|We are accounted|æstimati]], that is, reckoned and despised by persecutors and perverse men, [[8:36|as sheep for the slaughter|sumus ut oves occisionis]], that is, like sheep that are slain so that their wool and flesh may come to the use of those who slay them. Hence Christ too says to the disciples: [[Matt 10:16|Behold I send you as sheep in the midst of wolves|Ecce ego mitto vos sicut oves in medio luporum]]; and elsewhere: [[John 16:2|the hour cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doth a service to God|Venit hora, ut omnis qui interficit vos, arbitretur obsequium se præstare Deo]].

paras.t: Sed in his omnibus adversitatibus superamus, omnia patienter atque gaudenter sustinendo, propter eum qui dilexit nos, id est propter amorem Dei vel Christi, qui prior dilexit nos, et propter beneficium gratiæ ejus, cujus virtute hæc invictissime patimur.
paras.en: [[8:37|But in all these things we overcome|Sed in his omnibus adversitatibus superamus]], in all these adversities, bearing all things patiently and joyfully, [[8:37|because of him that hath loved us|propter eum qui dilexit nos]], that is, for the love of God or of Christ, who first loved us[[1 John 4:10||]], and because of the benefit of His grace, by whose power we suffer these things unconquerably.

paras.t: Certus sum enim quia neque mors, id est timor seu pœna mortis, neque vita, id est amor vivendi ; neque Angeli, qui sunt de infimo choro infimæ hierarchiæ cœlestis ; neque Principatus, qui sunt de supremo choro ejusdem hierarchiæ : et per istos subintelliguntur Archangeli, qui infra hos ordines sunt medii ; neque Virtutes, id est angeli de medio ordine secundæ hierarchiæ : per quos intelliguntur Potestates, quæ sunt de infimo ordine hierarchiæ secundæ. Numerantur autem horum ordinum angeli, quia sunt de quinque ordinibus angelorum qui foras mittuntur. Alii vero quatuor ordines adsistunt. Neque instantia, id est præsentia bona vel mala, neque futura prospera vel adversa, neque fortitudo, id est violentia alicujus, neque altitudo humanæ præsumptionis, neque profundum sapientiæ sæcularis, neque creatura alia poterit nos separare a caritate Dei, quæ est in Christo Jesu Domino nostro, id est, quæ secundum ejus doctrinam et voluntatem exhibetur a nobis Deo, ut eum toto corde, tota anima, tota fortitudine diligamus. Exhibitio enim beneficiorum caritatem accendit, nec aliquid sic ad amorem inducit, sicut quod aliquis scit et experitur se ab alio diligi. Quoniam ergo Deus tantam nobis dilectionem ostendit, tantaque beneficia contulit, debemus in ejus amore esse immobiles.
paras.en: [[8:38|For I am sure that neither death|Certus sum enim quia neque mors]], that is, the fear or pain of death, [[8:38|nor life|neque vita]], that is, the love of living; [[8:38|nor angels|neque Angeli]], who are of the lowest choir of the lowest heavenly hierarchy; [[8:38|nor principalities|neque Principatus]], who are of the highest choir of the same hierarchy: and by these are understood the Archangels, who are between these orders; [[8:38|nor powers|neque Virtutes]], that is, the angels of the middle order of the second hierarchy [*Virtutes*, the order of Virtues]: by whom are understood the Powers, which are of the lowest order of the second hierarchy. The angels of these orders are named because they are of the five orders of angels who are sent forth; the other four orders stand in attendance. [[8:38|nor things present|Neque instantia]], that is, present goods or evils, [[8:38|nor things to come|neque futura]], prosperous or adverse, [[8:38|nor might|neque fortitudo]], that is, anyone's violence, [[8:39|Nor height|neque altitudo]] of human presumption, [[8:39|nor depth|neque profundum]] of worldly wisdom, [[8:39|nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord|neque creatura alia poterit nos separare a caritate Dei, quæ est in Christo Jesu Domino nostro]], that is, the love which according to His teaching and will is shown by us to God, so that we love Him with our whole heart, our whole soul, our whole strength[[Mark 12:30||]][[Mark 12:33||]]. For the showing of benefits kindles charity, and nothing so draws to love as when one knows and experiences that he is loved by another. Since, then, God has shown us such great love and conferred such great benefits, we ought to be immovable in His love.

paras.t: Hoc dicit Apostolus in persona sui ipsius et Apostolorum aliorum quos sciebat confirmatos in gratia, ita quod mortaliter peccare non poterant, ab ea hora qua in die Pentecostes primitias Spiritus acceperunt. Vel si intelligatur dictum in persona omnium prædestinatorum, referendum est quantum ad separationem finalem. Nam licet aliquando per mortale peccatum separentur a Deo, finaliter tamen separari non possunt. Præterea quod de angelis dictum est, non est sic intelligendum, quod angeli sancti aliquo modo velint nos separare a caritate Dei ; sed ideo dictum est, quia etsi per impossibile vellent, tamen non possent. Secundum quem sensum dicit alio loco idem Apostolus : Licet angelus de cælo evangelizet vobis præterquam quod evangelizavimus vobis, anathema sit. Quidam vero per prædicta intelligunt angelos malos, qui nos conantur a Deo avertere. De quibus ad Ephesios legitur : Non est nobis colluctatio adversus carnem et sanguinem, sed adversus principes et potestates, etc. In Apocalypsi quoque scriptum est : Draco pugnabat et angeli ejus.
paras.en: The Apostle says this in the person of himself and of the other Apostles, whom he knew to be confirmed in grace, so that they could not sin mortally from the hour in which, on the day of Pentecost, they received the firstfruits of the Spirit[[Acts 2:1||]]. Or if it is understood as said in the person of all the predestined, it must be referred to final separation. For though at times they are separated from God by mortal sin, yet they cannot be separated finally. Further, what is said of the angels is not to be understood as though the holy angels in any way wished to separate us from the love of God; but it is said because, even if, per impossibile, they wished it, they still could not. In which sense the same Apostle says elsewhere: [[Gal 1:8|an angel from heaven, preach a gospel to you besides that which we have preached to you, let him be anathema|angelus de cælo evangelizet vobis præterquam quod evangelizavimus vobis, anathema sit]]. Some, however, understand by the aforesaid the evil angels, who try to turn us away from God. Of whom we read to the Ephesians: [[Eph 6:12|our wrestling is not against flesh and blood; but against principalities and powers|Non est nobis colluctatio adversus carnem et sanguinem, sed adversus principes et potestates]], etc. In the Apocalypse also it is written: [[Apoc 12:7|the dragon fought, and his angels|Draco pugnabat et angeli ejus]].
